title: test-0068-GEN-AIRQUALITY
passage: As winter settles over Delhi, residents are waking up to thick, grey smog. While many believe the air is safe if it looks clear or lacks a strong smell, invisible pollutants like PM2.5 are often present at dangerous levels. These tiny particles, much smaller than the width of a human hair, are far more harmful than larger PM10 particles because they can travel deep into our lungs and bloodstream. Many people mistakenly assume that staying inside a closed room provides total protection, but indoor air can also be affected by cooking or outdoor pollutants seeping in. Furthermore, while some think a simple cloth mask is sufficient, only certified N95 masks are designed to filter out these fine particles effectively. It is also a common myth that a city has one single AQI reading; in reality, air quality varies significantly between different neighborhoods and changes throughout the day. Relying on a few indoor plants to clean the air is not enough to combat high pollution levels. To stay safe, residents should monitor local AQI updates, avoid outdoor exercise on high-pollution days, and ensure their masks fit tightly to prevent unfiltered air from entering.
summary: Many people mistakenly assume that staying inside a closed room provides total protection, but indoor air can also be affected by cooking or outdoor pollutants seeping in.
